records.question: can you write me an essay about ivers portfolio

result.answer:
Iver Macaulay’s portfolio brings together practical AI, product development, and business automation. Across his work, he focuses on turning calls, files, and other business inputs into clearer information and useful next steps.

Mac Digital is a responsive website for digital services, with an interactive demo that turns a business prompt into a website concept with generated copy, optional imagery, and selectable layouts and typography. It also includes reduced-motion support and safeguards for generated output.

Drop It is a private library for saving screenshots, files, text, and links. Users can review AI-drafted summaries and transcriptions, organize saved material, and find it through keyword or optional hybrid search. It also includes account-scoped connections, portable backups, and recoverable Trash.

Amountly is an accounting workspace organized around bills, expenses, invoices, and tax preparation. Its documented product experience includes financial search and task-oriented workflows designed to help users focus on the next financial action.

One example of Iver’s automation work is an AI call intelligence pipeline. It transcribes RingCentral recordings, analyzes calls to assess lead quality and service details, and sends scored leads, transcripts, and related context to HubSpot. The workflow also guards against duplicate calls and records that are not valid leads.

Together, these projects show a portfolio centered on tools that fit into real workflows: creative website concepts, a library for saved screenshots, files, text, and links, clearer accounting tasks, and automated business processes. Iver’s stated approach is to make AI direct and dependable, and to have it move the work forward.

records.question: How can I spot a phishing email?

result.answer: Watch for unexpected messages that create urgency, ask you to click a link or open an attachment, request passwords or payment, or come from a sender address that doesn’t match who they claim to be. Don’t click; contact the organization through a website or phone number you already trust, and report or delete the message if it seems suspicious.
